scope: Exploratory finite-Hankel reduced operator calculus; no performance confirmation or manuscript change
numerical_revision: After retaining initial v1 results with failed reference checks, use Golub-Welsch Gauss weights and exact Jacobi ladder coefficients. Same cases, norms, tolerances and dimensions; v2 is authoritative only if original reference threshold passes.
kernel: K_m(x,y)=c sqrt(xy) J_m(cxy), L2(dx); phi=sqrt(x)*physical radial field
input_domain: Unit ball in the first r CPSWF modes, where r resolves K_m in spectral norm; external analytic inputs are checked separately
derivatives: Dimensionless Cartesian ladders: D+_m=d/dr-m/r takes m to m+1; D-_(m+1)=d/dr+(m+1)/r returns to m. No PDE boundary condition is imposed at r=1.
rank_policy: Scan every nested prefix; report first observed pass and full curves because final composite error need not be monotone
metrics: Spectral norm of intermediate leakage and final observation error, separately relative to each full reference operator. Raw coefficient density is descriptive only.
reference: Direct Bessel-kernel quadrature of analytic Jacobi derivatives/profiles; double source quadrature, larger output quadrature and padded commuting eigensolve audits
cost: Single-process phase times and retained array bytes are diagnostic only. No speedup claim; fresh-process paired confirmation is deferred until a useful algorithm is selected.
limitations: CPSWF and Hankel SVD are reusable across tested actions at fixed m,c; action SVD is rebuilt for every action and input rank. Source-domain restriction is not a general composite-operator approximation guarantee. SO(2) ladders are exact selection rules, not discoveries.
